title: Cleanup procedure: closed-task cleanup needs no approval round trip; native completion for hidden/partial content
outcome: Cleanup procedure: closed-task cleanup needs no approval round trip; native completion for hidden/partial content
acceptance: AGENTS.md 'Cleanup deletions' (and every repository instruction text that restates it, including CLAUDE.md's 'Work only in the repository folder' references) states that cleanup of a worktree, build output or temporary file whose served items are all closed needs no further approval from Greg, citing his verbatim word from TermAl mailbox 588693a8 #2781, while the existing pre-removal checks (absolute path inside the repository, no link escape, runs terminal with outcomes recovered, no live work, frozen input, shared resource or unique unpushed change) still apply.

The same section names a safe native Windows completion, only for a target whose served items are all closed and whose non-forced removal failed only because of hidden, read-only or partly removed content of that checked target: for a registered worktree, `git worktree remove --force <checked path>` with a single `--force`, and if its registration remains, it is left and reported; for a plain directory, `Remove-Item -LiteralPath <checked path> -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false`. Any other request for input or operational failure (such as a lock or a link escape) and any policy refusal still stop and are reported to the coordinator, and any other forced removal still needs Greg's recorded per-case authorization.

Both coordinators (Engram::Fable and Termal::Fable2) recorded concurrence on the exact wording, the wording was sent to Greg before landing, and the final-diff audit is recorded as passed; the Markdown-only link check passes on the clean candidate commit.
